details: On 29 Oct a quick gate of the git-could-not-answer branch (head 7aa0030d) went red on two tests with 143 != 0: a fixture gate script (echo ok; exit 0) was killed by SIGTERM from outside its own tree. Both tests pass alone, a rerun of the gate on 45188584 was green, and a fixer that logged every os.kill/os.killpg in a probe run saw no stray signal. Nothing in the gate records who sent a stop signal, so such a red cannot be explained after the fact and turns into a rerun (principle 6). A scout refuted the leak-scan overlap theory: run folders never nest (tests/run_unittest.py:18, tests/parallel_unittest.py:151, lib/relay_ci.py:124). Real shared state it found: the inert probe is not a session leader (lib/relay_ci.py:157), so it shares the outer bin/ci process group.
failing_case: tests/test_gate.py::test_f11_a_project_that_does_not_ignore_ci_can_run_the_gate_twice and tests/test_land.py::test_land_inert_take_reuses_gate red with 143 != 0 in a quick gate while each passes alone; the gate log does not say who sent the SIGTERM.
pass_cases: a test gate command killed by SIGTERM from another process leaves a line in the gate log naming the signal and, on macOS and Linux, the sender pid or 'sender unknown'
the inert probe runs in its own session: a SIGTERM to the outer bin/ci group does not reach the probe's tests, and the probe's stop does not reach the outer run
reason: tests/test_gate_stops.py::RunnerStopped::test_a_gate_command_ended_by_a_signal_leaves_a_line_in_the_gate_log passes and fails at e41418af (line absent). But the 29 Oct sender is still not found (see F2).
findings.summary: A gate test is stopped by an unknown SIGTERM

details: CONFIRMED by trace and reproduction. relay_ci.py:129 still says "relay gate SIGKILLs the group" as the reason the record
exists; the group kill was the only thing that ended the probe on that path, and the change removed the probe from the
group without giving relay gate (or reclaim) another way to reach it. Also the brief's own rationale does not hold: the
probe's stop used stop_tree over pids, never a group signal, so "the probe's stop could reach the outer run" was not a
real path before this change; the only group signal it adds is the new killpg in stop. And the process killed on 29 Oct
(a fixture gate command) already leads its own session, so the probe's group cannot have been the route (see F2).
Severity HIGH: ordinary use (stopping a gate) leaves an unbounded wait on the next gate of the worktree and a run outside
evidence: python3 -I gate2.py outer.py <branch worktree> repo sp
== branch: next gate CANNOT take the worktree lock: held by ['15955', '16034']
== master: next gate takes the worktree lock
python3 -I gate.py (ps of the probe after the group kill, branch):
80271 80271     1 SNs  sleep 600   -> "probe pid 80271 ALIVE after the gate killed bin/ci's group"; master: "gone"
lib/relay_gate.py:205-210  reclaim: members = {p.pid ... if p.pgid == group}; held = [pid for pid in holders if pid in members]; if not held: return False
lib/relay_ci.py:480-483   timer only when self.quick and not RELAY_INERT_PROBE
failing_case: `relay gate` on relay's own worktree is stopped while bin/ci runs (Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or SIGHUP to relay gate, e.g. a lane
stopped by the front or a hang bound). relay_gate.run's finally does os.killpg(bin/ci's pgid, SIGKILL): bin/ci dies with no
cleanup. Before this change the probe was in that group and died with it. Now (start_new_session=True) the probe and its
whole nested quick run keep running with ppid 1, holding the inherited worktree lock fd (close_fds=False), outside the gate
slot, and with no time limit (the nested run has RELAY_INERT_PROBE set, so Ci.main starts no watchdog). The next relay gate
of that worktree waits on the lock: reclaim only stops holders that are members of the group named in the lock file
(bin/ci's, now empty), so `held` is empty and it waits until the orphan's whole run ends (minutes; forever if it hangs).
Reproduced: outer process (own session) runs relay_ci.Probe with a sleeping nested command and inherits a flocked fd; the
"gate" SIGKILLs the outer group; on the branch the probe is alive (ppid 1, STAT SNs) and a new flock on the lock file
fails; on master the probe is gone and the lock is free. Should be: a stopped gate leaves no probe process and no held lock.
fix_hint: Simplest: drop start_new_session (back to the shared group; stop already ends the probe by pids) and remove the new killpg.
If the own session is kept: bin/ci must make every way it can die end the probe's group too, e.g. write the probe's pgid
into the lock file line ("<gate pid> <command group> <probe group>") and have relay_gate.run's finally and reclaim
killpg every listed group, or have reclaim stop all lsof holders of the lock whose gate pid is dead.
pass_cases: 1. A command run like relay_gate.run runs it (start_new_session=True, a flocked lock fd passed) starts a Probe whose nested
command sleeps; killpg(command pid, SIGKILL): within 2 s no process of the probe is alive and flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on
the lock file succeeds.
2. bin/ci stopped by SIGTERM (its handler raises SystemExit): Probe.stop runs, the probe and its children end, the worktree
is removed (works today, must keep working).
3. The quick watchdog (_stop_at_limit) still ends the probe with everything below bin/ci (works today).
4. A signal sent to the outer bin/ci group while bin/ci keeps running does not reach the probe's processes (the brief's
pass case), or, if the fix drops the own session, the item records why that pass case is withdrawn.
5. The F1 leftover test (test_ci_python.py:684) still passes: the next prepare() removes a killed probe's worktree, and no
probe process runs in a removed worktree.
reason: tests/test_ci_python.py test_a_group_kill_of_the_run_ends_the_probe_and_frees_the_lock passes (probe gone, flock succeeds); fails/hangs with the own session restored. Pass cases 2, 3, 5 covered by existing tests that pass; case 4 withdrawn with the own session (sibling test shows stop leaves outer group alone).
findings.summary: the probe in its own session survives relay gate's group SIGKILL of bin/ci, keeps the worktree's gate lock, and reclaim cannot free it

4. If the sender pid is recorded: on Linux, a fixture gate command killed by SIGTERM from a known helper process logs that

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Cheap to fix alongside F1. Size: 5.
evidence: tests/test_ci_python.py:583  self.assertEqual(os.getpgrp(), os.getpgrp())   # we are still here

details: PLAUSIBLE (small window, needs pid wrap). Disappears if F1 is fixed by dropping the own session. Size: 5.
failing_case: proc.wait() reaps the probe leader; when every member is already gone, the number proc.pid is free and a new process that
starts a session (every fixture gate command and test runner does) may get it before os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGKILL) runs; it
is then killed. This is the same class of stray signal (a signal to a number read earlier) the item hunts. Should be: the
group signal goes only while the group is known to exist (before the wait, or not at all).
fix_hint: killpg before proc.wait() (the zombie leader keeps the group number reserved), or drop it with the own session.
pass_cases: 1. Probe.stop on a probe whose children all ended: no signal sent after proc.wait().
2. Probe.stop on a probe with a child that left the tree but kept the group: that child ends.
reason: The post-wait killpg was removed in lib/relay_ci.py (stop no longer signals a group number).
findings.summary: Probe.stop SIGKILLs the probe's group number after the leader was reaped; an emptied group's number can be reused
